# Quality-first editorial rewrite loop

## Intent

As a publication operator (Anth.us newsroom, Chatticus marketing, or any Papyrus pod), I want an automated **editorial** loop that turns generic, low-information, overly uniform drafts into text with a real point of view, concrete evidence, appropriate uncertainty, and an audience-specific voice — so copy is substantively better, not merely “less detectable as AI.”

## Guardrail (non-negotiable)

This is a **quality** loop, not a detector-evasion loop. Do **not** optimize for “get below detector score X.” AI detectors are imperfect; NIST and related work warn that perplexity/burstiness-style indicators are not reliable evidence of human authorship. Do not inject fake typos, slang, manufactured anecdotes, or random fragments to game classifiers.

Track editorial outcomes instead:

- Fewer unsupported claims
- More concrete nouns, examples, numbers, attributable sources
- Less boilerplate and empty intensifiers
- Better audience fit
- Explicit trade-offs and uncertainty where warranted
- Document-specific voice match against approved reference writing

North-star metric: **human acceptance rate after factual review**, not detector score.

## Pipeline (diagnose → revise → verify)

Do not prompt one model to “humanize this.” Separate passes:

1. **Diagnose** — structured JSON findings (vague claims, empty lead-ins, uniform cadence, list-shaped prose, unsupported certainty, redundancy, voice mismatch). No prose rewrite in this pass.
2. **Retrieve** — author voice guide + project facts + prior approved copy.
3. **Constrained revision** — senior copy editor prompt; preserve meaning; no invented anecdotes/stats/citations; prefer deletion; style guide over generic Internet prose.
4. **Verify** — factual / style / redundancy checks; change log; unresolved questions.
5. **Acceptance gate** — accept revision only on net quality improvement and no new unsupported claims (weighted score: specificity, clarity, audience fit, voice match, minus redundancy / unsupported / factual-change risk).
6. **Human approval** — present a **diff**, never auto-publish externally attributable copy. Retain provenance (draft, each revision, model/version, retrieved sources, change log, human decision).

## Style profile

Derive an editable YAML (or equivalent) profile from 20–100 approved pieces: tone, sentence style, structure, prefer/avoid lexicon, evidence rules. For technical writing, favor operational detail (latency, cost, failure modes, constraints) over “transforming workflows.”

## MVP (narrow first)

1. Store an editable style profile + 5–10 reference samples
2. Diagnostic JSON pass
3. One constrained revision pass (draft + profile + diagnosis)
4. Verifier pass (factual changes, deletions, residual boilerplate)
5. Diff UI / handoff for human review (not auto-publish)
6. Log quality metrics over time (accepted revisions, deletions, unsupported-claim rate, reader edits, post-publication corrections)

## Out of scope

- Detector-score optimizers
- Fake imperfections / synonym spam / “personal” story inventing
- Auto-publishing without human approval for external copy
- Replacing Chattic.us-web `publication-writing` banned-phrase checks (those remain; this loop sits above or beside them as editorial judgment)

## Source seed

Operator brief distilled from a Perplexity research pass (quality-first editorial loop; NIST/synthetic-content caveats on detectors). Productize the brief; do not paste detector-evasion tactics into the skill.

## Children (MVP)

1. Style profile store + reference corpus (5–10 samples)
2. Diagnostic JSON pass (schema + checks)
3. Constrained revision pass (editor prompt + style profile + diagnosis)
4. Verifier + acceptance gate (score, no new unsupported claims)
5. Diff handoff + provenance log + human approval gate

# Quality-first editorial rewrite loop

## Intent

As a publication operator (Anth.us newsroom, Chatticus marketing, or any Papyrus pod), I want an **interactive** editorial loop that uncovers weak passages, offers rewrite options, and lets a human steer what gets changed — so copy is substantively better, not merely “less detectable as AI.”

## Guardrail (non-negotiable)

This is a **quality** loop, not a detector-evasion loop. Do **not** optimize for “get below detector score X.” AI detectors are imperfect; NIST and related work warn that perplexity/burstiness-style indicators are not reliable evidence of human authorship. Do not inject fake typos, slang, manufactured anecdotes, or random fragments to game classifiers.

Track editorial outcomes instead:

- Fewer unsupported claims
- More concrete nouns, examples, numbers, attributable sources
- Less boilerplate and empty intensifiers
- Better audience fit
- Explicit trade-offs and uncertainty where warranted
- Document-specific voice match against approved reference writing

North-star metric: **human acceptance rate after factual review**, not detector score.

## Human-steered loop (not a one-shot rewrite)

Machines do not “humanize this” into a new article. The loop is finding-level and option-level, with a human on the tiller at every apply.

Same pattern as reporting-packet review: machines produce private work products; humans record explicit decisions; nothing externally attributable is auto-published.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  draft[Working draft]
  diagnose[Diagnose: structured findings, no rewrite]
  steer[Human steers findings: skip, rewrite, delete, keep, add]
  options[LLM generates rewrite options for selected findings]
  choose[Human chooses, edits, or regenerates with guidance]
  apply[Apply chosen patches to working draft]
  verify[Verify applied draft]
  publish[Human approves before external publish]
  draft --> diagnose --> steer
  steer -->|"rewrite this"| options --> choose --> apply
  steer -->|"skip / keep / delete"| apply
  apply --> verify --> steer
  verify --> publish
```

1. **Diagnose** — structured JSON findings (vague claims, empty lead-ins, uniform cadence, list-shaped prose, unsupported certainty, redundancy, voice mismatch). No prose rewrite. Findings are the steering queue.
2. **Retrieve** — style profile + project facts + prior approved copy, used when generating options.
3. **Steer findings** — human marks each finding: skip, rewrite, delete, keep-with-note, or add a finding the machine missed. Batching is allowed; unattended full-document rewrite is not.
4. **Options** — for findings marked rewrite, an LLM produces two or three constrained **options** (patches), not one committed `revised_text`. Senior copy editor constraints: preserve meaning; no invented anecdotes/stats/citations; prefer deletion; style guide over generic Internet prose; no detector-evasion tactics.
5. **Choose** — human picks an option, edits it, rejects all, or regenerates with extra guidance. The working draft changes only when a human apply is recorded.
6. **Verify** — after apply, score the working draft (specificity, clarity, audience fit, voice match, minus redundancy / unsupported / factual-change risk). Verification advises; it does not auto-accept.
7. **Publish gate** — present a **diff** of original vs current working draft. External publish requires human approval. Provenance retains draft, findings, options, human decisions, model/version, and change log.

## Style profile

Derive an editable YAML (or equivalent) profile from 20–100 approved pieces: tone, sentence style, structure, prefer/avoid lexicon, evidence rules. For technical writing, favor operational detail (latency, cost, failure modes, constraints) over “transforming workflows.”

## MVP (narrow first)

1. Store an editable style profile + 5–10 reference samples
2. Diagnostic JSON pass whose findings a human can steer
3. Constrained **options** for human-selected findings (not one whole-document revision)
4. Verifier on the **applied** working draft (advisory; human still decides)
5. Diff + provenance of finding decisions, chosen options, and human apply/approve
6. Log quality metrics over time (accepted revisions, deletions, unsupported-claim rate, reader edits, post-publication corrections)

MVP steering surface: first-class decision records (files/CLI; Newsroom UI can come later). Do not bury steer/choose in an unlogged chat.

## Out of scope

- Detector-score optimizers
- Fake imperfections / synonym spam / “personal” story inventing
- Auto-publishing without human approval for external copy
- Unattended whole-document rewrite that a human only rubber-stamps
- Replacing Chattic.us-web `publication-writing` banned-phrase checks (those remain; this loop sits above or beside them as editorial judgment)

## Source seed

Operator brief distilled from a Perplexity research pass (quality-first editorial loop; NIST/synthetic-content caveats on detectors). Productize the brief; do not paste detector-evasion tactics into the skill.

## Children (MVP)

1. Style profile store + reference corpus (5–10 samples)
2. Diagnostic JSON pass (schema + checks) — findings are the steering queue
3. Constrained rewrite **options** for steered findings
4. Verifier on the applied working draft (advisory gate)
5. Diff handoff + provenance of human steer/choose/apply/approve
